desc:
AI follow-up support after training keeps new skills from fading. Ecom Swift LLC answers your team's questions by email, reviews how they use the tools, fixes common slips and suggests the next small step for a fixed starter period.

## What is AI follow-up support?

AI follow-up support is a set period of help that starts once your training or setup is finished. Your team sends questions in writing and we reply with clear answers and examples. We also look at real prompts and real uses, so the advice matches what people actually do and not what a course assumed.

It is a fixed starter sprint. Ongoing support beyond that is quoted separately, so you always know what is included.

## Why training fades without a check-in

People leave a workshop full of ideas and return to a full inbox. Within a few days, the first obstacle arrives: a result that looks wrong, a prompt that stops working, a tool setting nobody remembers. Without someone to ask, people quietly go back to the old way of working.

Questions that appear after training are the most valuable ones, because they come from real tasks. Answering them quickly turns a small frustration into a learned habit. Leaving them unanswered turns the training into an expense that never pays back.

## How support changes what your team achieves

Support improves adoption, and adoption is where the benefit comes from. A tool nobody uses saves no time. When a person gets a fast, practical reply, they try again, and each repeat makes the next one easier.

Reviewing real prompts adds a second effect. We spot patterns such as vague requests, missing context or copied results that were never checked. Pointing these out with a better version beside them teaches more than another lesson would. The size of the gain still depends on how much your team practises between replies.

## What good follow-up support includes

- A clear window during which questions are welcome by email.
- Written answers that include a worked example, not only an explanation.
- A reply within a stated working time.
- A review of real prompts or real uses taken from your team's own work.
- Notes on what is working and should be repeated.
- Fixes for common slips, such as pasting sensitive details into a public tool.
- Tips on what to change, written in plain words.
- A short progress note or call, depending on the package.
- A list of next steps for the following month.

## How the support period works

You give us a list of the people who will ask questions and tell us which tools they use. Your team then sends questions to us by email, one at a time or in batches. We answer each in writing, with a sample you can copy.

In the Basic package the focus is on written answers within a short window. Standard adds more questions and a review of a set of real prompts or uses, ending with a brief progress note. Premium covers a full week, a larger review, a check-in call and a written list of next steps. Add-ons include extra questions, an extra check-in call and a separate review of how the tools are used.

We can help with how to use a tool, how to word a request and how to check a result. If a tool itself is broken or needs a technical fix, tell us and we will explain what we can do within this service and quote anything beyond it separately.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Collect questions from the whole team and send them with the task they relate to.
- Include the exact prompt and the result you received.
- Tell us what you expected, so we can see the gap.
- Share a few real uses for review, with private details removed.
- Try each suggestion on a real task before asking the next question.

**Avoid:**
- Waiting until the support window is nearly over to ask anything.
- Sending only a screenshot with no description of the goal.
- Including customer names, contracts or other sensitive details in your questions.
- Expecting one answer to fix a habit without repeated use.
- Asking for a full rebuild of a tool within a question and answer service.

## Who this is for

This service suits a team that has just finished a workshop and wants help in the first stretch of real use. It suits a manager who introduced a tool and sees only two people using it. It also suits an owner who learned alone from videos and wants a second pair of eyes on how the tools are being used.

You do not need to have bought training from Ecom Swift LLC first. We can start from the tools and tasks your team already uses.

## What we need from you

A short note listing your team members, the tools in use and the main tasks they are trying to speed up. Then send questions by email as they come up. We never ask for passwords. If we need to see a tool, a screenshot or a shared example is enough, or you can add us as a limited team user where the tool allows it.
